name: Conversational uptake model
summary: A BERT model from Stanford that scores how much a teacher's reply builds on what a student just said, learned without labels from math classroom transcripts and checked against experts' ratings.
grades: not stated (trained on 4th and 5th grade math lessons)

license.note: Its card asks each user to agree to three terms before using it. The code and data in its GitHub repository are MIT (conversational-uptake).
license.terms: non-commercial use only; never try to recover its training data; don't share it beyond your research team and project

access_note: About 440 MB, not gated. Edu-ConvoKit 0.4.0 calls it ddemszky/uptake-model, which now leads here.
cite: Demszky, D., Liu, J., Mancenido, Z., Cohen, J., Hill, H., Jurafsky, D., & Hashimoto, T. (2021). Measuring Conversational Uptake: A Case Study on Student-Teacher Interactions. ACL 2021, 1638-1653. https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2021.acl-long.130

fits.how: Marks the turns where the AI builds on what the learner said: the Edu-ConvoKit component runs it on the person's own computer once they download it.

connect.note: Runs in the Edu-ConvoKit component's detector (edu-convokit) once you download it yourself. Its terms ask each user to agree not to share it, so nothing here fetches it. Trained on classroom talk; nobody has checked it on chats with an AI.
